case_studies.title: Reviving a 45+ year South Bay restaurant brand on social
case_studies.industry: Restaurant / hospitality (family-owned, 4 South Bay locations: Hermosa Beach, Redondo Beach, Palos Verdes, El Segundo)
case_studies.summary: Retainer social media management for a family restaurant group open since 1979. Clear Sky handles strategy, monthly shoots, editing, posting across 5 IG/FB pages plus TikTok and YouTube, community management, UGC outreach and ads. Recurring formats include the 'Cakes with Cris' interview series, staff trivia, and community PSAs (Strand Cam).
case_studies.challenge: From the internal client report: moderate social presence; TikTok weak overall; little online community interaction; no consistent color grade or brand palette in video; too much reliance on authority content and trends.
case_studies.approach: Once-a-month 6 hour shoot; 68 posts a month across 5 Instagram and Facebook pages (3 posts per page per week plus 20 videos a month for the main account); reposts to TikTok and YouTube; community management (comments, DMs); UGC outreach and collab management; monthly meetings; developing, launching and iterating on ads. People-first, humor and guest formats (Cakes with Cris with guests like Brook Billings, staff trivia, Surf Festival legacy story).
case_studies.results: Logged in the Notion Wins database: 'Volleyball Parallels' YouTube video (Jul 20, 2026) 28,276 views, 38.8x the 90-day organic median of 728. 'No Onions' IG Reel (Jul 8, 2026) 13,601 views, 9,632 reach, 63 shares. Realtor collab Cakes with Cris Reel (Jul 6, 2026) reached 10,333 accounts, 13,075 views; 4,467 Facebook video views. Strand Cam PSA Facebook Reel (Sep 2, 2026) 9,880 video views, 14.9x median. 'Viral Video' win logged Feb 26, 2026: 600K views. Sep 2026 social report: Instagram 19,037 followers, YouTube 14,800 subscribers, Facebook 6,352; August 2026 YouTube views were 268,726. NPS survey (Mar 10, 2026, Cris Bennett): 10/10 on all four questions. Southbay Magazine profile draft states the short-form videos 'have generated millions of views over the last two years.' Unverified sales claim in CCP course deck: 'We revived Good Stuff's page and after a year they had the best financial summer of their life' (no financial data found).
services: Earlier (2024 site copy): website, design, photography

Existing About drafts (verbatim sources, pick and edit):

1) Clear Sky About Us Feature (Drive, Aug 2026, https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ujTuf6H69pL9SB8uvgWaSA1P1YvJuvL34aS3XhR2bBg): "We live in an age where businesses with 100 million dollar & 100K dollar marketing budgets are going head-to-head on impressions. Social media has completely democratized creativity... As a smaller business, how do you compete with the people with seemingly limitless resources for attention, without having to pay for ad placement? That's where we come in. Clear Sky is a company that breathes digital content. We build our organic strategy around proven formats that are unique to your brand to build your ideal audience of motivated customers. On average, our businesses see 4x more impressions after three months of working with us... We have many ways to work with clients, from our free course, DIY consultation, all the way to full service management and growth, for both personal and business accounts."

2) Origin story (Clear Sky Brand Voice doc, Jul 2025, https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MWjyTUfMUgoC7__4RutI89d6qYm-BM7jQLZhdscXhMs): After college, Cameron, a lifelong baseball player and film major, saw MLB dreams fade and picked up a camera as COVID-19 pushed businesses online. While growing his comedy sports channel "Baseball Bro" to 50K+ followers and millions of views across platforms, he realized most businesses didn't know how to tell their story online, and Clear Sky Creations was born "to help founder-led brands authentically connect through video, story, and strategy." Six months into running Clear Sky full-time, a faith-driven heart-check reframed it as a mission "to build with integrity, transparency, selflessness, and love." Core values: Transparency, Integrity, Selflessness, Love, Focus. Mission: "Creating story-driven, faith-rooted media for visionary entrepreneurs because the digital world is flooded with noise, confusion, and mistrust. We humanize your brand with authentic content and ethical strategy."

3) Clear Sky New Direction (Drive, Jun 2025, https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AaGl0jD3LZsZ4rloGbGnGDkgJIaOpF6VfD-cEsZR0Jg): Mission "To bring integrity back to marketing and storytelling... Changed Companies Change Culture." Vision "Trailblazing the path forward toward honest marketing." Story: founder is a film graduate and former baseball player; pivoted from a viral personal content brand into a full-service marketing company dedicated to "branding with virtue"; "Rooted in Christian values but open to all"; "Over five years, Clear Sky has partnered with startups, MedSpas, restaurants, sports brands, and agencies."

Supporting facts: based in Long Beach, CA (3940 E Gilman St/Ave on invoices and contracts). Team bios from Topps treatment (Jun 2024): Cameron Bennett, Writer/Director (content in the baseball space for Adidas, Easton, Jack in the Box); Fidel Melara, Director of Photography (MLB, Baseballism, SeamsUp); Ryan Juarez, Post Production lead (prior roles at Marucci, Baseballogist, Perfect Game). CCP deck: Cameron has "10 years of experience in video production" and grew two niche accounts "to over 40K followers each". Note the follower figures differ across docs (50K+, 40K each, 35K TikTok + nearly 10K IG).

gaps: I found no finished, written case studies in Notion or Drive. The only 'Case Study' entries are a 2024 pricing-page mapping (CSC Web: Age With Vitality = DIY, Endera = Start Up, Good Stuff = Business, SeamsUp = Enterprise) and hero images in Drive. The 'Case Study' pages under each client portal's 200 Content Pillars are empty templates.

Most client compliments in the Wins DB are screenshots only, with no transcribed text: Good Stuff 'Compliment from Client' on reviews, 'Customer STOPS OWNER', Aesthetic Solutions 'I LOVE these videos!', Peachy 'Super Stoked Client', Calvary Chapel 'Fantastic Video'. Someone needs to transcribe them and get approval before they can be quoted.

NPS 'quotes' are short shout-outs, not testimonials. Before anything is published, get each client's approval and their preferred name and title. No long-form written or video testimonials from clients were found. The 'Testimonials - Case Study Interview Flow' doc and the Notion 'TESTIMONIAL/ CLIENT INTERVIEW TEMPLATE' pages are blank frameworks.
Google reviews are not stored in Notion or Drive. The 2024 revisions doc mentions only 2 five-star Google reviews.
The '4x more impressions after three months' claim (About Us Feature) has no supporting data in either workspace.
The D'Arnaud Athletics results conflict and have no data behind them: '4x their forecasted numbers after 6 months' versus 'six figures in the red ... profitable in just six months'.
The 'best financial summer of their life' claim for Good Stuff has no financial data behind it.

The Notion 'Origin Story' page (Company Information / Creations) is filled with AI template text: a 2019 corporate-job founding and 'One client noted a 50% increase in social media interaction'. It contradicts the real story (baseball and film, COVID era) and must not be used.
Follower counts for Cameron's Baseball Bro channel differ across documents: 50K+; 'two niche accounts to over 40K each'; and 35K TikTok plus nearly 10K Instagram.

The Meta 'Street Fair' ad results PDF (2025: 714,622 impressions, 21,190 link clicks, $3,783.64 spend, $0.18 CPC) sits in a Palos Verdes Chamber folder, but the chamber became a client in March 2026. It is unclear whether Clear Sky ran these ads, so I left it out of the case studies.

No outcome metrics were found for Endera, SeamsUp, 1736 Family Crisis Center, Evolus/Sona, RMC, Your Behavioral Health or LPI Products (Dog Horn / Shavemate TikTok Shop UGC campaign). The Downey Nissan 'Monthly Report' page is empty, and there is no documented pre-Clear Sky baseline for Downey or Good Stuff.

clients.notes: All 120 files are marked unverified. Checked read-only, nothing was changed. Sona Creative Group is a monday.com-first agency partner with sub-clients Evolus, Xtresse, Orange Twist and SprintRay, according to the Sona Client Workflow Template https://app.notion.com/p/3dda696c1a53819e8b3ec62d397b473f. That template also says Notion tasks only mirror monday items and are flagged Sona?. The Master Task Board has no Sona? tasks before March 2026, and every candidate file is from 2025 (Feb to Dec). The only Sona-linked Active Campaigns are Test Sona Project, Celia Xtresse (launched 2026-09-22, archived), Ad Board Raleigh (Oct 2026), the SprintRay Restore Documentary campaign (https://app.notion.com/3a7a696c1a5380c9adcfe7d4ccfd2ae1) and Company Culture Social Videos (Hugel). None of them matches Tarsus, The Skin Shop, Evolus NSM / Elite / Zero Bond / Evolux CBM, or the 2025 Xtresse Mastermind and Spring KOL edits. I searched task names (Tarsus, Evolus, Evolux, Skin Shop, Tiffany, Xtresse, Zero Bond, Aiyana, Elite, Mastermind, KOL, NSM, Role Play, String, Sculptra) and ran workspace searches; neither turned up a Notion record for these deliverables. The Final Deliverables database is empty. Approval status for this work most likely lives in monday.com (Sona Main Workspace), Clockify or invoices, not Notion. Drive invoices and Clockify reports for Sona 2025 exist but are billing records, not approval records, so they were not used. The Tarsus KOL Atlanta V9 files in the Revisions folder and the files named FINAL look final from their names, but Notion cannot confirm it. 2 further candidates were left out of the input list by the orchestrator and were not checked.
clients.inventory_notes:
I listed every subfolder of "*Sona Creative Group" and followed every nextPageToken until the result came back empty. Nothing was created, edited, moved, shared or deleted. Total: 145 files (144 videos, 1 Google Doc). There are no images, logos or project files. Paths are relative to the root folder. Every file had a size in the search results, so get_file_metadata was not needed.

Folders with nothing in them: SprintRay, Hugel, Evolus/2025/Evolux CBM/Mirror Mirror, and Xtresse/Celia Xtresse with its three subfolders (ProRes 422, Assistant Editing Exports, h.264). The Celia folders were created on 2026-10-12 and may still be uploading.

Duplicates: the Tarsus KOL Atlanta V4, V5 and V8 renders appear twice, once in the KOL Atlanta root and again in h.264. Both copies are marked not final because the V9 renders in h.264/Revisions replace them.

How I judged looks_final:
- Final: H.264 MP4 renders and the ProRes master in Final Exports, Stage Exports, Deliverables, Social Exports and h.264 folders, plus titled cuts with a version number.
- Not final: STRINGOUT and SELECTS files, which are raw camera or organised footage; versions replaced by a newer one in the same folder; and documents.

The best footage for a showreel is in these files: Evolus NSM Deliverables (recap, Career and F Word videos), Evolux Elite Event Recap V2, Tarsus NSM recap v3 and Hype Sizzle V2, Xtresse Spring KOL FINAL, and the Aiyana Atelier Vertical Ad.

clients.notes:
Read-only check; nothing in Notion or Drive was changed. Downey Nissan has 8 campaigns in Active Campaigns: March 26 (https://app.notion.com/320a696c1a5380f0bb86c9d82100b469), April 26 (https://app.notion.com/33da696c1a5380a69e47c4ac2eb43575), May 26 (https://app.notion.com/35ea696c1a538041815fcd3f9e051062), June 26 (https://app.notion.com/37ba696c1a5380e18db7fb12ab2c2413), July 26 (https://app.notion.com/398a696c1a538082b0dcc1a13d9a3dd4), and August to October 26. March to July are archived and every task in them is Done / 99.Completed.

There are no Notion campaigns for November or December 2025, so the 8 Nov/Dec OTT commercial files are unverified. Notion Deliverable Links point to Vimeo review pages, not Drive files, so most files are tied to a task by deliverable name plus campaign month. The exception is the 6 vertical commercials: the Done tasks "Commercial 1 Vertical" and "Commercial 2 Vertical" in the April campaign link straight to Drive folder 1GA0QGY8PXdx7LgGcuMSjQzUw6NJizyLy ("Verticals"). I confirmed through Drive metadata that the vertical files sit in that folder.

Version rule: when Drive has an older and a newer version of the same deliverable, only the newest is marked final_verified. That covers Can't Sleep and Pictures for MAX V1 vs V2, and two different "Soccer Commercial (Spanish)_April 8 V1" files with different timestamps. Some files with a V3 or V2 name have the same modifiedTime as the matching "_Final" file, so they are treated as the same render: Smartest Man Alive V3 and the 4th of July V3/V2 files.

No Notion task found for: Soccer Event Interview, Stop Recording Me, Top five CPO cars, the Spanish versions of Getting Hit by Car and Soccer Celebration (April 8; only English tasks exist), and Soccer Commercial April 29 V1 (16x9). Those are unverified. Also, 19 further candidate files were left out of the list given to this check and were not verified.
clients.inventory_notes: Read-only crawl; nothing was created, edited, moved, shared or deleted. I went through every subfolder and followed every nextPageToken. The connector returns only about 5 to 25 items per page even with pageSize 100. Total is 140 files: 138 MP4 videos, 1 AAC audio file and 1 drone stringout. There are no images, logos, documents or project files. Structure is Downey Nissan > November and December (2025 OTT commercials) and 2026 > March, April, May, June and July 26 x Downey Nissan, each holding an h.264 folder and a ProRes 422 folder. All five ProRes 422 folders are EMPTY, so only the H.264 delivery masters are on Drive. Every file sits under 03_Final Exports and is an H.264 MP4 render, so MP4s are marked looks_final=true. Names with an explicit 'Final' tag are the strongest signal: November OTT, July Commercials, the June 'Commercials' (Pregame Pep Talk / Test Tailgate) and the May verticals plus Smartest Man Alive. Other files only carry a version number (V1-V6); they are in the Final Exports tree but may not be the last approved cut. Exceptions: 'Drone Stringouts 7.1.26.mp4' (raw selects) and the AAC audio file are false. Duplicates (same size and modified time, different IDs): the December Baseball and Soccer commercials appear in both March/h.264/Commercials and March/h.264 root. The April 8 Baseball and Soccer spots appear in both March/h.264 and April/h.264/Commercials. Smartest Man Alive and 4th of July Savings each appear twice, 'Final' in May/h.264/Commercials and the 4th of July subfolder, 'V3' in April/h.264/Commercials. The folder months do not always match the campaign month in the filename (for example, May folder files tagged 'April 29', and July 'Commercials' files tagged May 26 and June 26). Best showcase candidates for the website: the 16x9 English/Spanish broadcast commercials, which are 'Final', larger files, and the latest are from July 2026.

clients.notes: Read-only check; nothing was created or edited in Notion or Drive. Vaya is in the Companies database with Status Dormant and Classification Through Agency. Its parent company is Sona Creative Group (https://app.notion.com/p/31ea696c1a5380c5a9e7c3ab903ebfaa). Per the CSC Notion map, Sona work runs through monday.com, and syncing that back to Notion is still unsolved. Searches found nothing tying these files to a Notion record: (1) No Active Campaigns rows have Vaya or Sona Creative Group as Company, and no campaign name contains 'Vaya' or 'Amazon'. (2) No Master Task Board task title contains 'Vaya' or 'Amazon'. The tasks containing 'Sizzle' belong to other clients' campaigns: Clash of Classes, a 2026 Sizzle Video (16:9), the Kim core content module, and the Welcome / Why Sizzle open video. (3) The Vaya Portal (https://app.notion.com/p/543a696c1a5382aaa2778111de77ae7e) and its Completed Deliverables page (https://app.notion.com/p/369a696c1a53821eba9e81387b13f4ff) only hold unfiltered template views of the Master Task Board, with no Vaya-specific records. (4) Workspace search for 'Vaya Amazon Edits', 'Vaya launch video shoot final exports' and '15 Second' found no matching record. The files are dated Feb to Nov 2025, before most of the current Notion task structure existed. Approval for them was probably tracked in Sona's monday.com board or in email, not in Notion. Every file is therefore unverified; none can be confirmed final or not final from Notion. The Drive folder names ('Final exports', 'FINAL OUTPUT SEQUENCE') and the version numbers in filenames (V7 to V9 sizzle, V2 to V4 15 second) suggest final status but are not Notion evidence. A next step would be to check Sona's monday.com board or Gmail threads with Sona and Vaya contacts.

clients.notes: Moonracer has no client, campaign or task record in Notion. Searches for "Moonracer" and "Moonracer LA County shoot" turned up only Daily Sales Checklist pages, and those describe Moonracer as outside the project system. The Sep 01 checklist (https://app.notion.com/p/3cea696c1a5381ac9437cac5a3fa7f83) says "Guardant ($1,880) and Moonracer Films ($1,400) paid you in 2025 and exist nowhere in Notion." The Aug 31 checklist (https://app.notion.com/p/3cda696c1a53817b982ed575c3c90635) and the Sep 02 checklist (https://app.notion.com/p/3cfa696c1a538102bc1adfd164c036ca) say Moonracer Films is a production company that hired Cameron as a camera operator for two days. These files are raw drone clips and stills (DJI_..._D_CSC) from that 9/23-24/2025 LA County shoot. That fits a camera-operator job where CSC handed over source footage and did not make edited deliverables. With no task or deliverable to tie any file to, every file is "unverified". notion_client_url points to the Aug 31 sales checklist because there is no Moonracer client page. Notion was only read: nothing was created, edited or commented on.
clients.inventory_notes: Read-only inventory; nothing was created or modified. The Moonracer folder (under 03_Final Exports) has one subfolder, "LA County Shoot 9.23 + 24" (id 1Qz_hcK3LqZKJG9kSzj65xpg34p6zMsub), and no other files or subfolders. Every page was followed to the end. The subfolder holds 49 files: 46 MP4s and 3 JPGs. They are DJI drone camera originals numbered 0147 to 0195 with none missing, shot 2025-09-23 and 2025-09-24, about 1.69 GB in total. The searches returned every size, so get_file_metadata was not needed. Every file keeps the camera's original name (DJI_<timestamp>_<seq>_D) with only a "_CSC" suffix added, and the subfolder is named for the shoot dates, not as an export. So all 49 are marked looks_final=false as raw drone footage and stills, even though the parent folder is 03_Final Exports. If the client was meant to get the raw drone files as the deliverable, they could count as delivered, but nothing in the names says they are edited renders. There are no project files, logos or documents.

clients.inventory_notes:
I only read the Drive folder and changed nothing. The client folder holds one project, "Hero Video Engagement", which follows the standard CSC structure (00_Pre Production, 01_Production, 02_Post Production). It has well over 300 files, so the list below is truncated.

What's left out of the list:
1. Raw camera footage in 01_Production/Raw Footage. Day 1 has about 100 video files, mostly Sony FX3 clips plus DJI drone MP4s with their low-res .LRF proxies and Insta360 .insv/.lrv files, and its list goes on to further pages I didn't read. Day 2 has at least 100 FX3 clips (0439 to 0543), and its list also continues. I list only a few sample clips. All of it is raw, so none of it is final.
2. Camera XML sidecars, about 1 per FX3 clip.
3. Audio: the 01_Production/Raw Footage/Audio folder (Zoom recorder WAV files 260624_0106 to 0116 with .bin files, plus more pages), 06_SFX, and the 04_Music/PreViz MP3s.
4. Screenshots and references, partly listed: 13_RMC Oxnard Facility has about 60 iPhone HEIC photos and MOV clips (IMG_5857 to IMG_5908) from a site scout. I list a few. The rest are scout footage, not final.
5. Premiere cache folders (Auto-Save, Audio and Video Previews, Captured and Generated) and 12_Proxy. These are cache folders; I didn't open them except 12_Proxy, which came back empty.
6. Pre-production planning folders that hold only documents (calendar, call sheets, permissions, forms, producing guide, a pitch deck template, and the misc folder). The 00_Up to Date folder is fully listed. 01_Old in 03_Working Exports came back empty.

Main findings:
- The 02_Final Exports/ProRes 422 and 02_Final Exports/h.264 folders came back empty. No file is labelled as a final deliverable.
- The newest full render is "Open House RMC.mp4" (785 MB, Oct 6 2026), in 03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date. I marked it looks_final because it is a finished MP4 render with no version or draft tag. It sits in a working folder, though, so confirm with the editor.
- The latest cut of the hero video itself is "Pre Viz_Hero Video Engagement_RMC V7.mp4" (667 MB, Aug 7 2026). Versions V1 to V7 plus two soundbite checks are all labelled Pre Viz, so I treated them as drafts.
- 02_Final Exports/Assistant Editing Exports holds full-size b-roll SELECTS reels (V2), interview string-outs (Dan, Johan) and a transcript. These are editing material, not deliverables. 01_Project Files/02_Assistant Editing Exports holds smaller copies of the same reels, plus a newer Aug 2026 string-out set.
- Logo: "Rep logo.png" in 01_Project Files/07_GFX. The 07_GFX/RMC_Styleframes-01 folder has 15 motion-graphics styleframe PNGs (SHOT1 to SHOT10 plus KEY1/KEY2).
- 03_Client Assets holds AI-generated images and clips (Gemini and other generators) plus reference media. In 04_Music/PreViz, the corporate videos from other companies (Nicro, Bossplast, JA Brooks and similar) are third-party reference clips, not RMC work.
- The search tool usually returned only about 5 results per page even when asked for 100. I followed nextPageToken in every folder except the large raw footage and audio folders and the pre-production document folders, where I stopped early on purpose.
- Sizes come straight from the search results, so I did not need get_file_metadata.

clients.inventory_notes:
READ-ONLY inventory. Nothing in Drive or Notion was created, edited, moved, shared or deleted. Only search_files was used. Every file already had a size, so get_file_metadata was never needed.

SCALE: This tree holds well over 300 media files once raw footage is counted. It has 7 client folders (Evolus, SprintRay, Orange Twist, Xtresse, Vaya, The Skin Shop, Guardant, Omada, House RX, Joya, Evolux) and dozens of projects, each in the CSC template (00_Pre Production / 01_Production / 02_Post Production, plus 00_Project Files / 01_Footage / 02_Final Exports / 03_Working Exports). I enumerated about 330 files and then stopped, so truncated=true.

WHERE THE DELIVERABLES LIVE: Almost every "02_Final Exports" folder (with its h.264, ProRes 422, Assistant Editing Exports and Split/Mix subfolders) is an EMPTY template. The real delivered renders sit in "03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date" as versioned files named "<Deliverable>_<Project>_<Client> V#.mp4". So looks_final=true marks the HIGHEST version of each deliverable in 00_Up to Date, plus anything explicitly named Final, TV Export, Youtube, or sitting in a non-empty Final Exports folder. Older versions in 00_Up to Date and in 01_Old are looks_final=false. Most superseded versions were left out of the list on purpose to save space; they are counted in the skip list below.

Exception: Evolysse B&A Edits is the only project whose 02_Final Exports/h.264 folder actually holds files.

BEST PORTFOLIO CANDIDATES (all MP4 unless noted):
- SprintRay Restore Documentary: V13, Final Youtube, plus a launch trailer and 15/30/60 second social teasers.
- Orange Twist: CTV spots (General / Filler / CoolSculpting, with and without QR) and the Twist X Sizzle V2.
- Evolus Zero Bond: event sizzle and 6 doctor presentation videos.
- Evolus Evolysse B&A Edits: 8 talent edits.
- Evolus Jeuveau Elite: 3 Mother Daughter spots.
- Evolus CBM practice content series: Aesthetic Solutions, UnionDerm, Vivid Beauty Clinic, NoBe, CALM Tyler TX, Alyssa S / Forever Young, Ariel Ostad.

MISFILED: "Social Reel 1-7_UnionDerm SCC" files sit inside Zero Bond/03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date.

SKIPPED / NOT ENUMERATED:
1. All 01_Footage, 01_Production, 00_Pre Production and 00/01_Project Files folders (raw camera footage, proxies, project files). The only exceptions are 2025 NSM (one 33GB CAM1ISO recording seen; its Stage Cams subfolder was not opened) and Evolysse BTS (4 iPhone MOVs seen).
2. About 60 superseded V1 to V(n-1) renders across the Evolus CBM, Restore, Orange Twist, Zero Bond and Jeuveau projects. They were seen but left out of the list.
3. Xtresse post-production export subfolders for these projects were never opened: 2026 NSM, 2026 NSM Opening Tuesday Sizzle (only its 02_Post Production root was read, which yielded the .aep listed below; its 02_Final Exports and 03_Working Exports were not opened), AAD Recap Edit, Dr Levine Social Content, Hairstylist Program, UTC Westfield Tour de Xtresse, Leavitt and Curico, Fashion Island Activation, Social Content Development, Trill Educational 2.24.26, MOA, ASDS, Miami Event, Mastermind Coverage, Xtresse Xvie Lab, Mercury Dallas Mastermind, Spring KOL 25, Ad Board Raleigh. These may hold more finals.
4. Other folders not opened: The Skin Shop/Injections by Tiffany Event exports; Omada (Fall Campaign/BTS Edit/Projects, VoiceOver Debbie, Song Choices, Existing Footage); House RX/Annual Retreat Content exports; Joya; Guardant; Evolux/Evolux Summit 2026; Vaya/Amazon Edits exports and Animated Projects Old/Assets/AE files.
5. Inside projects that were read: Zero Bond Presentation String Outs (Proxy); Restore V8 and V10 Audio Mix folders; Arielle Template / Soo Update subfolders; Evolysse Clinical Video old exports; Midas Dallas footage; University of Evansville Production; Twist X 01_Old.
6. Several first-level folder listings returned a nextPageToken that was followed. The batched OR-of-parentId queries returned no tokens, so I treated them as complete.

clients.notes: I checked Notion only and changed nothing. The company page (Status: Dormant) has no Active Campaigns linked to it. I searched Active Campaigns for 1736, Crisis, Spring, Poker and Chase and found no 1736 campaign. The only hit, "Chase d'Arnaud Content Sprint", belongs to a different company. I also searched the Master Task Board by task name (1736, Poker, Chase, Crisis, Lower Third, Graphic Pack, Brand Book, Brand Story, Spring Marketing, Fundraising, Gala, Carol) and by Deliverable Link (these Drive IDs, "00_Up to Date"), and found no 1736 tasks or deliverables. The client portal's "Completed Deliverables" view is an unfiltered template view of the Task Board, not a list for this client. The Final Deliverables database is empty. Related context exists but ties to no specific file. (1) The Fathom meeting "1736 catchup chase x carol x cam" on 2026-01-16 (https://app.notion.com/p/387a696c1a5381c1bb8bef005051b0a8) says the brand story video was still in final revision before the Feb 7 event, with a new "Chase edit" planned. That is a status for a single brand video and cannot be tied to Chase Video 1 to 6, which were exported 2025-05-26. (2) The production team meeting on 2025-08-26 (https://app.notion.com/p/25ba696c1a5380c4a866f9e943e316cc) says Spring Marketing Push was awaiting asset uploads. (3) Notion search also returned the SOW Google Doc, which is outside Notion. It marks the brand identity refresh as COMPLETED, but that is not a Notion record and is not tied to individual files. Because no Notion task, campaign or deliverable record for 1736 exists, every file is unverified. The main session could check Vimeo or Drive Final Exports to confirm delivery.
clients.inventory_notes:
I only read files. Nothing in Drive or Notion was created, edited, moved, shared or deleted. I did not fetch either website.

Folder structure. The root has three subfolders: "Spring Marketing Push" (2025), "Video Ads" (empty) and "Poker Tournament" (Feb 2026 event). I walked every subfolder by parentId. Two things to know about paging: the API returned a nextPageToken on almost every page, and following it usually gave an empty result. The ARW photo folder also returned pages that overlapped each other.

Main finding: the "Final Exports" folders are empty. Spring Marketing Push > Post Production > 02_Final Exports > ProRes 422 > Split is empty, and Poker Tournament > 02_Post Production > 02_Final Exports (h.264, ProRes 422, Assistant Editing Exports) is empty too. The best stand-ins for finished CSC video are "Chase Video 1-6.mp4" in 03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date. These are MP4 social cuts from May 2025, about 66-109 MB each. Every other CSC video here is raw footage or a string-out. The Poker Tournament has raw footage and RAW photos only, with no edit or export yet.

Finished graphics: the 300ppi PNG exports (Lower Third, Graphic Pack, Asset 1/2), 1736 Logos.svg and the Brand Colors PNG/PDF. Note that 00_Project Files/00_Client Assets/Videos holds about 30 finished videos the client supplied (gala, PSA, testimonials from 2018-2025). These are the client's own archive, not CSC work.

What I left out of the list (this is why truncated=true):
(1) Poker Tournament/01_Production/Photo: about 180 or more Sony RAW .ARW stills (1CP08980-1CP09185, 14-32 MB each, uploaded 2026-02-17), all raw and not final. I listed 3 samples.
(2) Poker Tournament Video/02.07.26 1736 Poker Event (Video)/Cam A: about 100 or more raw CS_A_20260207_*.MP4 clips (100 MB-1.5 GB each). Cam C has at least 1 large clip (CS_B_20260207_6692.MP4, 8.6 GB). The Audio folder has raw WAVs (260207_001/002 Tr1/Tr2). Cam B was not fully paged. I listed 5 samples.
(3) Spring Marketing Push/01_Footage Day 1 and Day 2 camera folders (FX3, A7SIII, A7IV Chase/Subject, Lav, Boom First Kid Interview): raw camera originals from Dec 2023, not opened file by file.
(4) About 60 Premiere Auto-Save .prproj files and the Audio Previews .PRV folder.
(5) 8 Musicbed licensed music WAVs (03_Music), 5 Chase SELECTS/Video denoised MP3s (08_Misc) and 2 aegraphic lower-third templates.
(6) Poker Tournament/00_Pre Production: generic CSC template paperwork (about 30 release/agreement DOCX files, call-sheet and budget templates, Reese Hopper pitch-deck templates, calendars, "What goes in this folder.rtf"). None of it is media.
(7) Idea Boards v3/v04 package Fonts folders and duplicate PSD links (DVMbsq.psd, NKYsDU.psd, canstockphoto cropped.psd).

Sizes all came from search_files, so I never needed get_file_metadata.

clients.notes: I matched the client to the Active Campaigns entry "Dog Horn Social Launch" (https://app.notion.com/31fa696c1a5380e3b18ee0de20098d3f; Launch Status: Successful Launch; Email Subject Tag: LPI // Dog Horn Launch). It has 18 video tasks on the Master Task Board, and I could match 17 of them to files by title. None of the video tasks is Approved or Done, so no file is final_verified. 16 tasks are Paused in Phase 07.Social Media Management, which suggests post production was handed off, but no completed status was ever recorded. "Discovered a mysterious cooler in the woods." is in External Review with the note "client not sure on this". "Viral Hook Alt 3" has a client Notes Round 1 entry (Lou, Aug 11: the product name is never said), Client Revision Log 1, and Needed Phases back to 05.Post Production, so it is not final. "Behind the curtain" is Stuck ("waiting for assets") and no file matches it. The milestone "Posting live on the brand account by Sep 28" is Paused ("Delayed, waiting on clients"). The milestones "All 30 CSC videos delivered and approved" and "All 60 videos delivered and whitelisted" are still Proposed. Deliverable Links on the tasks point to Vimeo review pages, not Drive files, so the matches rely on title and version. Where a task's Version # field shows a later version than a file, I marked that file not_final as superseded. Older versions of tasks with no Version # field are unverified. Raw footage, found footage, SFX, music, GFX and screenshots are source material with no deliverable record, so they are unverified. I made no writes in Notion or Drive. 9 further candidates were omitted from the input and were not checked.
clients.inventory_notes:
READ-ONLY inventory; nothing was created, edited, moved, shared or deleted. Structure: LPI Products > Dog Horn Social Launch > {00_Pre Production, 01_Production, 02_Post Production}. The search tool returned only 5 results on many first pages despite pageSize 100, so nextPageToken was followed on every page. The folder holds well over 300 files, so videos and images were prioritised and some files are summarised here instead of listed one by one.

KEY FINDINGS:
(1) 02_Post Production/02_Final Exports and all of its subfolders (Assistant Editing Exports, ProRes 422, h.264) are EMPTY. 03_Working Exports/01_Old is also empty.
(2) All rendered deliverables are 35 MP4s in 02_Post Production/03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date. They cover 17 concepts with versions V1, V2 and V3 (TikTok vertical cuts). The newest version of each concept is marked looks_final=true. Older versions are marked false because a later version replaces them. Newest versions: V3 of "Let me tell you about the product", "For Bears, Coyotes, and Bobcats" and "Viral Hook Alt 3". V2 of "One tool that will save my life", "Finishing up my hike", "Discovered a mysterious cooler", Viral Hook Alt 1/2/4, This vs That Alt 1, No more gatekeeping Alt 1/2/3 and Loves Their Pet Alt 1/2. V1 of Training Alt 1/2, which have only a V1.
(3) 01_Production/Raw Footage/8.10.26/Contents holds 5 copies of V1 exports. They were parked in the raw folder and are superseded.
(4) The latest Premiere project is "Dog Horn Social Edits_Melvin.prproj" (modified 2026-09-21).

(a) 01_Production/Pictures: 94 Sony RAW stills, CSC04387.ARW to CSC04487.ARW (a few numbers missing), about 34-35 MB each, all modified 2026-04-28. Only 3 samples are listed. All are raw and not final.

clients.notes: I checked Notion read-only and made no changes. None of these files can be verified as final from Notion. The client is the Company record YourSLPsister (321a696c...), which started on 2026-03-12. Its only campaign is "March 26 x YourSLPsister" (https://app.notion.com/p/322a696c1a538048a40bd26df6cd4ad2, CSC-38, Clear Sky Social, archived, launched 2026-03-12, Google Drive Folder empty). I found no Master Task Board tasks linked to that campaign. The only SLP-related tasks are onboarding admin items under campaign 353a696c... ("YourSLPsister", "Complete Company page for YourSLPsister"; Done, no Deliverable Link) and "Recover to NAS: March 26 x YourSLPSister" (https://app.notion.com/p/3eda696c1a5381968024e1334cbe16da). That last one is a Done folder-restore task under an internal campaign, not a deliverable approval. Every file in "SLP Sister OLD" is dated Nov 2025 to Feb 2026, earlier than any Master Task Board record for this client (the oldest is 2026-03-13). The older SLP Sister Playbook Content Database (collection://310a696c-1a53-8194-aa20-000b51b55c84, which has Approved Edit and Posted fields) has no rows. The Final Deliverables database only has Name and Client fields, and I found no SLP rows linked to it. Searches for Pet Shop, Reaction (Deaf, Monkey), Sick Season, Reading a Story, Millie, Rattle, Swing, Shadow, Nature Play, Tag, Race and Model Play found no matching tasks. "Loves Their Pet Format Alt 1/2" belongs to another client's campaign (31fa696c...) and does not match. The looks_final flags (highest version number in an Edits folder) are filename guesses that Notion does not confirm. Proof of approval would have to come from elsewhere, such as Slack, email, Frame.io or Vimeo review links, or Metricool post history.
clients.inventory_notes: Read-only crawl of SLP Sister OLD, with every subfolder searched and every nextPageToken followed. 136 files in total: 131 videos (95 raw iPhone MOV clips and 36 rendered MP4 edits) and 3 Google Docs of notes and text overlays. There are no images, logos or project files. These folders are empty: Thumbnail Pics, B-Roll Clips/Dani, both Curated Content/(Template) folders and their Edits/Footage subfolders. Sizes came from search results, so get_file_metadata was not needed. The folders have no Final or Export subfolders. Edits sit in "Edits" folders and are named <Title>_SLP SIster_V#.mp4, so looks_final=true marks the highest-numbered version of each piece. Older versions, including everything in Edits/Old Versions, are false. One exception: "Taking Turns, Pretend_SLP SIster_V1.mp4" has no later version but sits in Old Versions, so it is false and flagged. Raw MOVs whose names start with "*" (e.g. "*tag fun.MOV") look like source clips picked for editing, not deliverables. Probable final deliverables: Petshop_V2, Reaction To Deaf Video V3, Reaction to Monkey V2, Sick Season V2, Reading a story V4, Millie V3, Tag Fun V1, Race Fun V3, Nature Play Educ V2, Millie Model Play V2, Shadow Educ V2, Swing Fun V2, Rattle Fun V2. "SIster" is misspelled in the original filenames. Several duplicate raw clips exist, e.g. IMG_6122.mov appears 3 times in Reaction to deaf video, and the "Copy of IMG_*.MOV" files in Nature duplicate files in Millie. Nothing was created, edited, moved or shared.

clients.notes:
I checked Notion read-only and made no writes. I could not mark any file as final, so every file is "unverified". The Ottawa Ford School Bus shoot and edits ran from Jul to Oct 2025. That is before the current Notion system was set up: the Master Task Board and Active Campaigns records start around Mar 2026. Here is what I checked:
(1) The Endera Motors company page (Status Active) lists no campaign for this project.
(2) An Active Campaigns query on the Endera company, "Endera" or "Bus" returned nothing.
(3) The Master Task Board has only two Endera tasks, and neither is about these files: "Endera Motors" (https://app.notion.com/p/31ba696c1a5380d797f9c252ef40118f, a client research report under the Leah Onboarding campaign, Done) and "Landing Page (16:9) x Endera" (https://app.notion.com/p/3a0a696c1a53803594acf3ffe816a3d0, Done, Jul 2026, delivered via Vimeo and unrelated to these files).
(4) The Final Deliverables database is empty.
(5) The Endera portal's Completed Deliverables view (view://404a696c-1a53-82e4-88dd-881939291585) returns no rows.
(6) No task's Deliverable Link contains any of these Drive file IDs.
The only Notion record of this project is a meeting note from Aug 26, 2025 (https://app.notion.com/p/25ba696c1a5380c4a866f9e943e316cc). It says the Ottawa Ford School Bus Video had its sign replacement done but still needed color grading and audio fixes, which Furkan was assigned to do. That means the bus video was not final on Aug 26, 2025. It does not say which version was approved; Bus Video V6, modified Aug 29, 2025, came after that meeting. Based on the folders and version numbers, the likely finals are Facility Video _10, Bus Video V6, and the FX3 PNGs and DJI JPGs in 02_Final Exports/Photos, but Notion does not confirm any of them. Delivery emails or a Vimeo or Frame.io review would be the way to confirm.

All files are listed for these folders: 03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date (16 MP4 cuts), 02_Final Exports/Photos/FX3 (20 PNG stills), 03_Client Assets, 07_GFX, 02_Assistant Editing Exports, Additional Clips and the main project files.

Partly listed:

- 11_Sourced Footage/Additional BTS: video sample only.

- Premiere audio/video preview caches: not recursed.
- 08_Luts/CSC LUTS: not recursed.
- 04_Music (4 Musicbed WAVs) and 09_Misc (4 MP3s): not listed.
- Pre-production template documents (release forms, call sheets, pitch deck templates, calendars): not listed.

Other notes:
- 02_Final Exports/ProRes 422 (Split/(Deliverable Name), Mix) and h.264 contain no files, so no final video master exists in Final Exports.
- The latest edit cuts are in 03_Working Exports/00_Up to Date: "Facility Video_..._Endera_10.mp4" (Oct 1, 2025) and "Bus Video_..._Endera_V6.mp4" (Aug 29, 2025). These are the most likely delivered videos. 03_Working Exports/01_Old is empty.
- Some Premiere preview folders mention a different project, "Wasko Delivery", so files from another project are mixed in here.

There is no separate "D'Arnaud Athletics" company. That company has two campaigns, "Content Sprint" (created 2026-07-09, https://app.notion.com/p/398a696c1a5380e0acdcdfbd1b8fc1b8) and "Chase d'Arnaud Content Sprint" (created 2026-08-03, https://app.notion.com/p/3b1a696c1a53808eb00cdb622a797a26). The tasks in both campaigns are 2026 work: Scripting, call sheets, Mookie LGND Glove Launch Event, editor wrap up, and similar. None of them refer to the Website Hype Videos, the January 2025 social clips, Facility Walk Through, Hitting Lesson, DA Clip Database or Summer Camp '25.

I searched the Master Task Board titles and deliverable links for Hype, Facility, Walkthrough, Middle/High School, JP Crawford, backhand, GOAT, Rushmore, Summer Camp, Hitting Lesson and the Drive file IDs. Every match belonged to another client or was an internal task. I also searched the whole workspace for the January 2025 clip titles (breathing, Mount Rushmore, Destroy phone, JP Crawford) and found no tracking records.

The "Chase D'Arnaud Playbook" Content Database (collection://313a696c-1a53-81c7-af1b-000b5e3d1ed1) has columns for Approved Edit, Approved for Posting and Posted, but it returned zero rows. The current Mission Control system dates from Feb 2026. These files date from Dec 2024 to Jul 2025 (Hitting Lesson as early as Mar 2024), so their approval status was likely tracked somewhere that is no longer in Notion, possibly Vimeo review links or email.

One side reference exists. The Master Task Board training page "Kim: Core Content module" (https://app.notion.com/p/3dba696c1a53816fae90d1b5f3d3a8e6) uses "Tour of the Facility_March_D'Arnaud Athletics_V6" (vimeo.com/1067927730) as an editing example. That suggests a later V6 of the facility video exists on Vimeo, beyond the Drive "Facility Walkthrough_V2". It does not show an approval status, so it proves nothing about finality.

Result: no Notion record shows a completed, approved, delivered or published status that can be tied to any of these files. Every file is "unverified". The "looks_final" flags come only from folder and version naming. To confirm them, check Vimeo review approvals or client emails from Feb to Mar 2025.
